name: Aubrey Miller
story: Aubrey Miller is a University of Otago geospatial educator and practitioner. Otago identifies him as a Senior Professional Practice Fellow teaching GIS, spatial analysis, programming and remote sensing, managing the Spatial Software Laboratory and convening GIS@Otago. The 2018 New Zealand Esri User Conference also records his presentation on moving BIM information into GIS for three-dimensional use.

Cartographies of change: GeoCart 2018 proceedings, National Library of New Zealand record 40158196 lists Aubrey Miller as an author of “Dissecting the GPS track”; “Tracking the transformation of camping in New Zealand”; “Local farm knowledge mapping for heritage and biological research”.
GeoCart session 1 programme, New Zealand Cartographic Society (archived programme page) lists Aubrey Miller as an author of “Banks Peninsula subtidal habitat mapping”.
GeoCart 2024 session 3 programme, New Zealand Cartographic Society lists Aubrey Miller as an author of “Digital Geomorphology: Repeat UAV Lidar Mapping of Aoraki/Mount Cook’s Changing Landscape”.

Aubrey Miller staff profile: NZGRC 2022 Matariki Project proceedings citation, University of Otago lists Aubrey Miller as an author of “The Matariki Project: 3-D change detection with satellite photogrammetric mapping”.
